title: Nostalgic Peppery Mexican Wensleydale Mole Poblano
description: A smoky, peppery mole blended with creamy Wensleydale and topped with crisp pumpkin seeds, ideal for a lazy Sunday dinner.
instructions: Roast poblano peppers over an open flame until skins blacken, then place in a bowl, cover, and let steam for 10 minutes before peeling and slicing.
Heat olive oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat and sauté diced onion and carrot until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add chopped tomato, smoked paprika, black pepper, cocoa powder, and honey to the skillet; cook for another 3 minutes, stirring frequently.
Pour in vegetable broth, bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, and let it reduce for 10 minutes to concentrate the flavors.
Transfer the sauce to a blender, blend until smooth, then return it to the skillet and heat through, stirring occasionally.
Stir in shredded Wensleydale cheese until melted and the mole thickens to a glossy consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt if needed, then remove from heat.
Spoon the mole into a lacquerware bowl, topping with chopped cilantro, toasted pumpkin seeds, and a scattering of tortilla chips for added crunch.
Let the dish rest for 5 minutes so the flavors meld and the chips crisp up slightly.
Serve warm as a comforting, peppery main course for a lazy Sunday dinner.
